Honest UK prices

What hosts charge guests vs what cleaning actually costs

Two different numbers get mixed up in most guides. The cleaning fee is what a host charges the guest on the listing. The turnover cost is what the host pays the cleaner. Here are both, from published 2026 data — all third-party estimates, not official statistics.

Where hosts are searching

Turnover cleaning, area by area

Changeover work looks different in a Notting Hill terrace and a Cotswolds cottage. Pick your area for the details that matter locally — then build a request pack written for firms who actually cover it.

London

London turnover cleaning

29,056 active Airbnb listings (AirROI, trailing 12 months to Sep 2026) compete for a limited pool of reliable cleaners. The median fee hosts charge guests is £56 — £68 across Greater London — so there is room to pay a good firm properly and still cover the cost in the fee. Congestion, parking and key logistics shape quotes here more than the clean itself.

Manchester

Manchester turnover cleaning

City-centre apartment blocks drive Manchester's short-let market: football weekends, arena nights and corporate stays mean short, frequent changeovers, often same-day. Most blocks need fob access and booked loading bays — put both in your request pack so firms can quote without a site visit.

Edinburgh

Edinburgh turnover cleaning

Festival season compresses a huge share of Edinburgh's changeovers into August, and Old Town tenements add stairs, shared closes and tricky key handovers. Book festival cover months ahead, and remember Scotland runs its own short-term-let licensing scheme — check your licence status alongside your cleaning contract.

Bristol

Bristol turnover cleaning

Harbourside flats, Clifton townhouses and family homes near the Downs make up Bristol's mix, with strong weekend and university-visit demand. Terraced streets mean permit parking — a cleaner who knows the zones will quote keener than one pricing in ticket risk.

Cotswolds

Cotswolds holiday-let cleaning

Cotswold cottages are bigger, older and further apart: more bathrooms, wood burners, boot rooms and longer drives between jobs. Firms price in travel time across villages like Kingham, Broadway and Bourton-on-the-Water, so a realistic per-clean budget sits above a city flat's — the estimator's “rural & holiday areas” setting is the honest starting point.

Seaside turnover cleaning

Brighton, Portsmouth (median guest fee £40), Cornwall and the Norfolk coast all share the same pattern: a short, intense summer season, sand and salt in every clean, and changeover day falling on the same Saturday for half the street. Off-season, ask about winter deep cleans and damp checks between lets.

The three add-ons hosts ask for

Same-day turnovers, linen hire & checkout cleans

10:00 out · 15:00 in

The standard same-day window: five hours to strip, clean, launder or swap linen, restock and photograph the property.

Same-day turnovers

Back-to-back bookings are where ratings are won and lost. A same-day specialist works the fixed window between checkout and check-in, flags damage with timestamped photos before the next guests arrive, and keeps a buffer stock of linen at the property so a late laundry run never delays a clean.

  • State your exact checkout and check-in times in the request pack
  • Expect a premium over a standard changeover — the estimator adds one when you tick “same-day”
  • Peak Saturdays book out first; secure cover before you open the calendar

Linen hire for Airbnb hosts

Washing, drying, ironing and storing three sets of linen per bed is the hidden workload of hosting. Linen hire replaces it: hotel-standard sheets, duvet covers and towels delivered before each changeover and the used set collected — no machines running at midnight, no airing cupboard full of spares.

  • Usually priced per bed or per changeover, on top of the clean
  • Ask firms to quote clean-only and clean-plus-linen separately
  • Pairs with same-day turnovers — fresh linen arrives with the cleaner

Checkout cleans (the standard changeover)

The core service behind every figure on this page: the full reset between one guest leaving and the next arriving. A proper checkout clean is a checklist job, done the same way every time, and finished with photos — which is exactly what the request pack asks firms to confirm they provide.

  • Beds stripped and remade; bathrooms sanitised; kitchen including fridge, hob and bins
  • Floors vacuumed and mopped; surfaces, mirrors and touch-points wiped
  • Restock basics, check for damage and left items, report with photos

Host checklist

The turnover checklist to hand your cleaner

Print this page or copy the checklist into your request pack. Agreeing the list up front is what turns a one-off clean into a reliable recurring standard — and it is what the top-rated listings quietly have in common.

Every changeover

  • Beds stripped, remade with fresh linen
  • Bathroom sanitised — loo, shower, taps, mirror
  • Kitchen — hob, worktops, sink, fridge emptied & wiped
  • Bins emptied, fresh liners, recycling out
  • All floors vacuumed and hard floors mopped
  • Touch-points wiped — handles, switches, remotes
  • Restock: loo roll, soap, washing-up liquid, tea & coffee
  • Damage & left-items check, photos sent to host

Weekly / every few stays

  • Oven and hob deep clean (specialist add-on — median £120)
  • Inside windows and glass doors
  • Descale kettle, shower head and taps
  • Skirting boards, light fittings, cobwebs
  • Washing machine and dishwasher filters
  • Check smoke & CO alarms, replace batteries
  • Inventory count — glasses, cutlery, hangers

Seasonal / between lets

  • Carpet and upholstery deep clean
  • Mattress protectors washed or replaced
  • Damp and mould check, especially seaside properties
  • Garden, patio and bins jet-washed
  • Boiler service and safety certificates in date
  • Re-grout and re-seal bathroom silicone if stained
  • Review guest feedback for recurring complaints

Know before you host

Short-let rules that affect your cleaning calendar

Cleaning is an unregulated trade in the UK — anyone can offer it, which is why references and a written checklist matter. The rules below are about the letting itself, and they shape how many turnovers you can legally run.

In force — London

The 90-night rule

Under the Deregulation Act 2015, a London home can be let on a short-term basis for up to 90 nights per calendar year without planning permission. Beyond 90 nights you need permission from your borough council. Airbnb applies the cap automatically to London listings unless you evidence permission — plan your turnover budget around the nights you can actually sell.

Coming — England

Short-term-let registration scheme

The government has been developing a registration scheme for short-term lets in England. At the time the research behind this page was compiled (October 2026) it had not yet come into force — registration was pending, with details still to be confirmed. Watch for it: registration may become a condition of listing, and it is separate from any local planning rules.

Scotland differs

Scotland's licensing scheme

Scotland already runs a licensing scheme for short-term lets, and Edinburgh has additional control-area rules. If your property is in Scotland, your cleaning arrangements sit alongside a licence — keep the licence number in your request pack so firms know the property is properly authorised.

Good practice

No licence needed for cleaners — vetting still matters

Because cleaning is unregulated, there is no official register to check a firm against. Ask for references from other hosts, public liability insurance, a written per-changeover checklist, and a clear policy for damage reporting and key holding. The request pack below prompts for all four.

Questions hosts ask

          
Airbnb cleaning FAQs

          

            

              How much does an Airbnb turnover clean cost in the UK?
              
Worked examples for UK hosts put a typical turnover clean at £55–£60 per changeover (Houst, 2026 guide). Exact prices depend on property size, bathrooms, location and whether linen hire and restocking are included, so treat any online figure as an estimate and confirm it with local firms.

            

            

              What cleaning fee do London Airbnb hosts charge guests?
              
AirROI's 2026 UK data puts the median cleaning fee charged to guests at £56 in London and £68 across Greater London. Elsewhere the medians are lower — £50 in Essex, £41 in Nottingham and £40 in Portsmouth. The fee you charge guests and the amount you pay a cleaner are two separate numbers; keeping the first at or above the second is what makes the maths work.

            

            

              How many turnovers will my property have each year?
              
A managed two-bedroom flat in Houst's 2026 worked examples runs 70–110 turnovers a year — roughly 6 to 9 changeovers a month. Your own calendar, minimum-stay rules and seasonality will move that number up or down.

            

            

              What is included in a turnover clean?
              
A standard changeover covers stripping and remaking beds, laundry or a linen swap, bathroom sanitising, a kitchen clean including the fridge and bins, floors throughout, restocking basics such as toilet roll, soap and tea and coffee, and a damage and left-items check with photos. Oven deep cleans, carpet cleaning and inside windows are usually priced as add-ons — an oven clean costs a median of £120 (Airtasker UK, 2026).

            

            

              Can I get a same-day turnover clean?
              
Yes — many firms specialise in the checkout-to-check-in window, typically guests out at 10:00–11:00 and the next in at 15:00. Same-day cover usually costs more and books out first in peak season, so state your checkout and check-in times clearly when you request quotes, and secure cover before opening peak dates.

            

            

              Is linen hire worth it for a small host?
              
Linen hire gives you hotel-standard sheets and towels delivered per changeover, with no washing machines, drying space or spare-set storage at the property. It is usually priced per bed or per changeover on top of the clean. Ask firms to quote cleaning-only and cleaning-plus-linen so you can compare like for like.

            

            

              What are the rules for short lets in London?
              
Under the Deregulation Act 2015, a London home can be let short-term for up to 90 nights per calendar year without planning permission; letting beyond that needs permission from the local council. England also has a short-term-let registration scheme in development that had not come into force when this page was researched (October 2026). Rules differ across the UK — Scotland has its own licensing scheme — so check your local position.

            

            

              How does this site make money, and is my data stored?
              
The estimator and request pack run entirely in your browser — the details you type are not uploaded or stored by this page. The site is a free host resource; when local firm matching launches in an area, firms may pay a flat fee per verified request they receive. Prices shown here stay estimates from the published sources listed below, whoever you end up booking.
